questions.answer: Um, so, a key assumption in the direct collocation method for optimal control is that, um, the system dynamics can be represented in a way that, like, you can break them down into discrete points or intervals. questions.question_text: What is an open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer:
Um, okay, so open-loop control in deterministic problems is like a control method where you, um, you decide on a sequence of actions or inputs ahead of time without really adjusting based on what happens after you start. So, like, you have this model that tells you how to change the system, and you just follow that plan. 

I think it’s tied to optimization because you’re trying to find the best actions that minimize or maximize something, right? In deterministic problems, everything is predictable, so you can just stick to your plan without needing feedback. But, um, if something unexpected happens, this method might not work so well. So, it's kind of simple but has its limits.

questions.question_text: What is an open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer:
Um, okay, so open-loop control in deterministic problems, I think, is like a way to manage or control a system without feedback. So, um, you start with a clear model of how the system works, and then you decide on a sequence of actions to take, based on that model. 

In a deterministic context, it means that if you know the initial conditions and your actions, you can predict exactly what will happen next. So, um, it’s kind of like just setting a course and not adjusting it based on what happens afterward. I guess it’s really tied to optimization because you sort of optimize your actions beforehand, right? But, um, I'm not totally sure about all the details.
